label: third original token, right after a "b" at position 1
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, almost entirely at step t=2 (99.3% of activation mass) when the previous input (orig token 1) was "b". The input token at t=2 itself barely matters, apart from "x", which shows about twice the rate. The strongest activations (max) come from sequences starting "b b x". Activations are lower when the first token is a digit or some letters (e.g. 2 b 3, q b u ~0.15-0.25 of max). It is silent at the delimiter, during the copy phase, at t=0, and after a b at any other position. Tiny residual activity (<1% of mass) shows up at t=1 after a leading b and at t=3 for b b b. False positives are mostly t=2-after-b steps with certain first tokens (v, l, x, c); excluding those raises dev F1 from 0.90 to 0.94, but that rule was left out as ad hoc.

issues: Systematic false-positive class based on the first token. On dev, the precision of the predicate (prev_tok==b)&(t==2) split by orig(0) is 1.0 for 25 of the 30 first tokens, but 0.0 for n (553 predicted), v (594) and x (545), 0.036 for c (507), and 0.718 for l. These five tokens account for nearly all of the 2322 test false positives. This is a clean token-identity gate, not noise, so calling the exclusion 'ad hoc' and leaving it out is unjustified.

The explanation's list of suppressing first tokens is wrong. It names v, l, x, c but leaves out n, which is fully suppressed (precision 0.0). l is only partly suppressed: with first token l, the feature still fires for most third tokens (a, d, e, l, n, v, x, 0 all have precision 1.0) but not for b or c.

Adding the exclusion: (prev_tok==b)&(t==2)&~isin(orig(0),[c,n,v,x]) raises test precision from 0.859 to 0.989 and test F1 from 0.898 to 0.964, while recall (0.941) and mass recall (0.993) stay the same. The label 'right after a b at position 1' therefore overclaims, because it ignores the condition on position 0.

Minor: the residual activity at t=1 is not 'after a leading b' in general. It is specifically the sequence 'b x' (t==1 & prev b & in_tok x: precision 1.0, 501 steps) and the activation is about 0. The t=3 'b b b' residual is real but tiny (mass 0.007). The claims about phase and position (silent at the delimiter, in the copy phase, at t=0 and at t>=4; 99.3% of mass at t=2) check out.
skeptic.revised_label: third original token (t=2) right after a "b" at position 1, unless the first token is c, n, v or x

final_label: third original token (t=2) right after a "b" at position 1, unless the first token is c, n, v or x
